original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a nonlabel technology that can detect, monitor, and quantitatively measure intermolecular interactions in real time.15, 16 The interactions between compounds 15, 21, 22, 35, 38 and FXa were evaluated by SPR assay. On the one hand, the results of inhibitory activity were verified to avoid the difference brought about by the single detection method; on the other hand, more binding information of the small molecule compound and the FXa target was obtained, it is beneficial to the further optimization. The sensorgrams and kinetic parameters of the interactions were shown in Figure 1 and Table 2.
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Fig. 1. The sensorgrams of compounds 15, 21, 22, 35 and 38 by SPR
original_paragraph.Table 2: Table 2 Kinetic parameters of the interactions between different compounds and FXa by SPR | Compound | k_a (M⁻¹·s⁻¹)a | k_d (s⁻¹)b | K_D (M)c | |----------|----------------|------------|----------| | 22 | 1.93×10⁴ | 1.45×10⁻¹ | 7.52×10⁻⁶ | | 35 | 1.84×10⁴ | 1.56×10⁻¹ | 8.44×10⁻⁶ | | 38 | 1.88×10⁴ | 1.87×10⁻¹ | 9.98×10⁻⁶ | a association rate constant (k_a); b dissociation rate constant (k_d); c affinity (K_D = k_d/k_a).
original_paragraph.Sensorgram Data (Figure 1): The sensorgrams in Figure 1 show the relative response (RU) over time (s) for compounds 15, 21, 22, 35, and 38 at concentrations of 0.63 µM, 1.25 µM, 2.50 µM, 5.00 µM, and 10.00 µM. The x-axis ranges from -50 to 100 seconds, and the y-axis ranges from -5 to 10 RU. The association phase occurs from approximately -50 to 50 seconds, followed by a dissociation phase from 50 to 100 seconds.
